query: Across Type of Traveller and Class, which review themes are associated with higher vs. lower Overall Rating?

per_column.name: crew_attentiveness
per_column.rationale: A well-distributed thematic axis that lets the analyst relate crew experience to Overall Rating across traveller type/class. Values track the source text well in the samples (welcoming crew -> exceptional_proactive). Slight risk of inference when text is silent, but samples are sound.

per_column.name: food_quality
per_column.rationale: Genuine theme axis with good distribution and reasonable NULL rate for silent rows. However, sample 2 mentions nothing about food yet was labelled poor_disappointing, an unwarranted negative inference where 'unknown' was appropriate; this drags groundedness.

per_column.name: seat_comfort
per_column.rationale: Largely redundant with the existing original 'Seat Comfort' rating column, reducing new analytical leverage, though the categorical framing adds mild qualitative texture. Values match source text (narrow/poor padding -> cramped_uncomfortable).

per_column.name: aircraft_condition
per_column.rationale: A new theme axis not present in originals, useful for grouping. High NULL rate correctly handles silent rows. But sample 2 says nothing about aircraft age/condition yet was labelled comfortable_aging, an invented specific; minor groundedness hit.

per_column.name: customer_service
per_column.rationale: Heavily overlaps with crew_attentiveness and the original 'Staff Service' rating, largely restating the same signal. Sample 2 labelled 'slow' with no service comment in the text is unsupported.

per_column.name: value_for_money
per_column.rationale: Directly redundant with the existing original 'Value For Money' rating column, adding little new axis. Sample 2 labelled fair_reasonable despite no value/price mention is a weakly grounded inference.

per_column.name: class_premium_decline
per_column.rationale: A relevant flag for the Class dimension of the query, offering a distinct grouping axis. But the true/false judgement (premium experience declining) is often not derivable from short review text and risks confident assertions where the text is silent; groundedness is uncertain.

judge.rationale: Several added columns (crew_attentiveness, food_quality, aircraft_condition, class_premium_decline) provide genuine thematic axes well suited to relating themes to Overall Rating across traveller type and class. However, seat_comfort, customer_service, and value_for_money substantially restate existing original rating columns or each other, limiting new leverage. Groundedness is generally good with appropriate NULLs for silent rows, but multiple columns over-assert negative/specific labels on rows where the source text is silent (notably the seat-only review in sample 2), indicating a tendency to hallucinate confident values rather than abstain.
